invariant: DescriptionDiagramFactory command regexes are compiled through Pattern2.compileInternal with CASE_INSENSITIVE. Every spelling of a CommandCreateElementFull.ALL_TYPES keyword therefore selects the same USymbol and Entity type, and CommandPackageWithUSymbol treats container keywords and AS case-insensitively as well. Case changes affect neither identifier spelling nor label text, package ownership, constructor order, layout dimensions, nor SVG geometry.
causal_divergence: Rust has two internal product paths that render Java DESCRIPTION diagrams. The deployment parser captures uppercase element keywords with a generic word regex but tests them directly against a lowercase DEPLOYMENT_KEYWORDS set. The component-backed DESCRIPTION path uses case-sensitive strip_prefix matching in container_keyword. Subtype detection can therefore route a complete source to the correct DESCRIPTION surface while whichever internal parser owns that grammar silently drops uppercase or mixed-case DATABASE, QUEUE, or BOUNDARY lines. This removes real nodes and corrupts package dimensions, SVEK layout, canvas size, and paint order. The defect is command-token normalization at both parser boundaries, not symbol geometry or dispatch scoring.
planned_change: ASCII-case-fold only captured or compared command keywords before lowercase family membership and semantic kind dispatch in both DESCRIPTION parser paths, while preserving identifiers and labels verbatim. Make optional AS tokens case-insensitive in bare and quoted declaration forms. Add family-spanning parser tests for uppercase and mixed-case leaf/container declarations in the deployment and component-backed paths, then rerun the dispatch follow-up-3 DESCRIPTION pairs exactly. Do not change layout constants, symbol renderers, comparator behavior, or SVG output after rendering.
perturbation_axes: uppercase, lowercase, and mixed-case element keywords
bare identifier versus quoted display and AS alias forms
